claims.text: Ultrasonic burnishing of a FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix will improve its overall wear resistance relative to an untreated coating.
The wear-resistance improvement will persist across varied thermal and contact regimes.
Ultrasonic burnishing causes severe plastic deformation in the coating.
The burnishing-induced deformation refines grains in the coating.
The burnishing-induced deformation causes dislocation accumulation in the coating.
Grain refinement and dislocation accumulation increase coating hardness.
The hardness increase produced by ultrasonic burnishing contributes to improved wear resistance.
Ultrasonic burnishing will reduce the wear rate of FeNiCrCoCu coatings on Cu.
The wear rate will decrease by at least 60% relative to the untreated coating.
Other medium-entropy-alloy coatings have shown better wear resistance after ultrasonic burnishing than corresponding untreated coatings.
The magnitude of the wear-resistance improvement may depend on the ultrasonic-burnishing parameters and test conditions.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a wear-rate decrease of at least 60%, but the rejection rule only requires that the treated coating fail to achieve a statistically significant decrease. A smaller but significant decrease could therefore fail the quantified prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
